notes: Focused v1.9.0 interaction-guidance regressions for #74: the Esc/q/Ctrl+C quit ladder, scrolling and position, selection stability under live data, log follow mode, text input and multi-line submit, tree views, modal geometry, emoji width in columns, the mouse default, and diff views. Assertions define the grading rubric; improvement claims require a recorded harness run against one immutable skill hash. Status (2026-10-27): recorded. Baseline and with-skill runs on Claude Code and Codex, three repetitions per case, are in evals/results/v1.9.0-claude-comparison/ and evals/results/v1.9.0-codex-comparison/ against skill tree 164c1aefd956.

evals.name: quit-ladder
evals.prompt: My nested TUI uses Esc for five different things and q quits from anywhere. What order should Esc, q, and Ctrl+C follow?
assertions: Gives an ordered Esc ladder: cancel the running operation, close the topmost overlay, clear the filter or search, go back one level, and do nothing at the root
Says each Esc press takes only the innermost applicable step
Says Esc never quits the app
Says q goes back in nested views and quits only at the root, and that q is a letter while a text field owns input
Says Ctrl+C cancels a running operation first and otherwise quits, with a second press to confirm when work would be lost
Confirms a quit only when it loses something (unsaved edits or running work), with a default of No, and never asks on an idle quit

evals.name: follow-mode
evals.prompt: I'm adding a live log viewer to my TUI. How should auto-scroll behave while the user reads?
assertions: Follows (pins to the bottom) by default when opened
Pauses following on any upward scroll and holds the viewport still
Shows a pending-lines indicator such as '37 new' while paused
Re-pins with G (jump to end) or F (toggle follow)
Caps retained lines with a ring buffer and says when the oldest lines were dropped
Offers a wrap toggle, rather than always wrapping or always truncating

evals.name: selection-stability
evals.prompt: The process list in my TUI refreshes every second and the cursor keeps jumping to different rows. How do I fix it?
assertions: Tracks the selection by a stable ID rather than a row index and re-resolves it after refresh, sort, and filter
Moves to the nearest surviving neighbor, not the first row, when the selected item disappears
Keeps the selected row at the same screen position when rows are inserted or removed above it
Does not re-sort on refresh unless the user changed the sort
Offers a freeze or pause key shown in the footer, with a PAUSED marker and a count of pending changes

evals.name: multiline-submit
evals.prompt: My chat TUI's input field should send on Enter but let users add newlines. Shift+Enter doesn't seem to work in some terminals. What should I do?
assertions: Explains that Shift+Enter is distinguishable from Enter only with the kitty keyboard protocol or similar enhanced keyboard reporting
Falls back to Alt+Enter or Ctrl+J for inserting a newline
Tells users the newline key in the placeholder or footer
Makes pasted newlines insert newlines instead of submitting (bracketed paste)

evals.name: text-input-keys
evals.prompt: Which editing, history, and completion behaviors should the text field in my agent TUI have, and how do I handle Tab?
assertions: Supports arrows, Home/End, and readline-style aliases such as Ctrl+W, Ctrl+U, and Ctrl+K, without making them the only route
Notes that Ctrl+A collides with GNU screen's prefix
Recalls history with Up and Down when the cursor is on the first or last line
Accepts dimmed ghost-text suggestions with Right or End
Resolves the Tab collision: a field that completes owns Tab, and focus moves another way

evals.name: scroll-keys
evals.prompt: Which scrolling keys and position indicator should my list view have?
assertions: Includes PgUp/PgDn, Ctrl+U/Ctrl+D for half a page, and Home/End or g/G
Keeps a scroll-off margin of a few rows between the cursor and the viewport edge
Shows a position indicator such as 42/1,203 or a percentage
Treats a scrollbar as optional and does not rely on it alone

evals.name: tree-keys
evals.prompt: What keys and behaviors should a tree view in my TUI have?
assertions: Uses l or Right to expand (moving to the first child if already open) and h or Left to collapse or move to the parent
Shows a per-node loading spinner for lazily loaded children
Keeps expansion state by node ID across refreshes and filters
Keeps the ancestors of matches visible and expanded while a filter is active

evals.name: modal-geometry
evals.prompt: How wide should confirmation dialogs be in my TUI, and how do I show a modal when NO_COLOR is set?
assertions: Sizes the modal to about 60-80% of the terminal width with a sensible maximum, centered
Allows one modal at a time
Clears the cells behind the modal instead of letting text show through
Does not rely on dimming alone to signal modality: uses a border, title, and changed footer hints that survive NO_COLOR

evals.name: emoji-columns
evals.prompt: My table has a status column with ⚠️ and ✅ and the columns misalign in some terminals. Why, and what do I do?
assertions: Explains that emoji built from a narrow base plus a variation selector or joiner (such as ⚠️) render as 1 or 2 cells depending on the terminal and width library, while Wide-base emoji such as ✅ take 2 cells
Recommends narrow text symbols or words for status columns
Says to use a grapheme-aware width measurement and test on target terminals if emoji are kept

evals.name: mouse-default
evals.prompt: Which mouse reporting modes should my full-screen TUI enable, and should my inline picker use the mouse?
assertions: Enables modes 1000, 1002, and 1006 for a full-screen app with click targets, not 1003 unless hover effects need it
Provides an off switch for mouse capture
Leaves the mouse off in inline tools
Keeps every mouse action reachable from the keyboard

evals.name: diff-view-choice
evals.prompt: How should my TUI show diffs on both a 100-column and a 160-column terminal?
assertions: Chooses unified view on narrower terminals and side-by-side on wide ones, with a width threshold around 120 columns
Marks changed lines with + and - in a gutter column, not by color alone
Provides hunk navigation keys
Does not wrap lines in side-by-side mode
